question.text: A compound is formed by substitution of two chlorine for two hydrogens in propane. The number of possible isomeric compounds is

solution.text:
$\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_8 \stackrel{-2 \mathrm{H}}{+2 \mathrm{Cl}}>\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_6 \mathrm{Cl}_2$, following isomers of $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_6 \mathrm{Cl}_2$ is possible
Due to presence of chiral carbon compound (IV) is optically active and forms an enantiomer. So total no of isomers $=5$
